composing_text: Panzer Regiment 3; Panzergrenadier Regiment 2; Panzergrenadier Regiment 304
current_activity: marching from Amiens toward the battle area
notes: Began move from Amiens to the battle area night of 9-10 June; on 10 June strung out between Amiens and Alencon, not expected in strength until 13 June; arrived without tanks at first.
Counter-attacked 13 June between Cahagnes and Villers-Bocage with two infantry regiments and two artillery battalions but no tanks.

current_activity: 2nd Panzer Division attack toward the Brécey-St. Hilaire road stopped at le Mesnil-Adelée
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 463: the main effort in the center; the right column rolled through le Mesnil-Tôve to le Mesnil-Adelée, where just west of the village it met resistance that forced a halt shortly after daybreak, 7 August, three miles short of the initial objective; the left column advanced through Bellefontaine and almost to Juvigny. Location: le Mesnil-Adelée, the place where the right column was halted. Location caveat: the left column stopped near Juvigny; the point is the right column halt. Opponents: American artillery and antitank pieces north and south of the Sée River kept the wedges immobile (p. 463); elements of the 3d Armored and 30th Infantry Divisions were identified in the zone (ch. 24 p. 461).

current_activity: 2nd Panzer Division armored elements reach St. Lambert about 1000; Luettwitz leads an attack across the Dives bridge
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 548-549: the corps order reached the division about 1900 on 19 August; Luettwitz held off until 0400, 20 August; only the armored elements and part of an armored infantry regiment reached St. Lambert in good order about 1000, and Luettwitz led an attack across the river into the village over the Dives bridge. Location: St. Lambert (Saint-Lambert-sur-Dives). Opponents: Allied artillery fire descended on the columns when the fog lifted (p. 548-549).

source_locator: R393: p. 177-178; R643: listing under the XLVII Panzer Corps heading
current_activity: The 2nd Panzer Division makes the initial penetration for the XLVII Panzer Corps by a bridge at Dasburg
notes: Event date: CMH Ardennes ch. 8 p. 177: "The initial penetration by the corps' right was charged to the armored infantry of the famous 2d Panzer Division (Colonel Meinrad von Lauchert)"; p. 178: "Once the 2d Panzer Division had thrown a bridge across the Our at Dasburg"; Nafziger 944GLAA (15 December 1944): "2nd Panzer Division: Oberst M. von Lauchert". Event definition: the opening of the offensive on 16 December. Event support: two source families: CMH and Nafziger. Location: Dasburg with a precision of 5 km, the bridge site named. Location approximate: a village point. Location support: CMH names Dasburg. Commander: Oberst Meinrad von Lauchert. Opponents: US VIII Corps (28th Infantry Division, 110th Infantry).

location_qualifier: the Seventh Army sector along the Our; the division position is not named
current_activity: 2d Panzer Division, severely depleted, turns south with the XLVII Panzer Corps to help the Seventh Army
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 2 p. 50: "Field Marshal Model at Army Group B provided help by ordering first a Kampfgruppe, then all that was left of the Panzer Lehr Division, transferred from the Fifth Panzer Army"; p. 51: "the XLVII Panzer Corps with the 2d Panzer and Panzer Lehr Divisions cutting across the grain of the withdrawal to go to the Seventh Army's aid". Event definition: the traffic of 22 January described on p. 51; the order itself came a few days earlier and is undated. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Vianden with a precision of 25 km, the Our crossing area where the Seventh Army needed help; the division position is not named. Location approximate: a representative point for the Seventh Army sector at the Our. Location support: CMH names the Seventh Army sector at the Our. Commander: unknown. Opponents: US 5th and 80th Infantry Divisions.
